source_text:
κόσμου τούτου προσκυνεῖν μήτε ἐμπολιτεύεσθαι, τί ἀνέχεσθε τῶν δογματιζόντων
ὑμῖν κατὰ τὴν τοῦ κόσμου τούτου πολιτείαν ὡς κατ' αὐτὴν ζῶντες; τί ὡς ζῶντες ἐν
κόσμῳ δογματίζεσθε· μὴ γεύσῃ, μὴ θίγῃς, μὴ ἅψῃ· ἅ ἐστι πάντα εἰς φθορὰν τῇ
καταχρήσει; ταῦτα ὡς δόγματα Ἑλληνικὰ ἐκτίθεται· παραγγέλλουσι γὰρ οὗτοι ἐν τῇ
ἰδίᾳ πλάνῃ μηδὲ ἅπτεσθαι μηδὲ γεύεσθαι παντὸς ἐμψύχου. πάντα γὰρ ταῦτα ἐδόθη
τοῖς ἀνθρώποις εἰς φθοράν, οἷον ἐπὶ τῷ φθείρειν αὐτὰ καὶ καταναλίσκειν ἐν τῇ
ἀποχρήσει καὶ τῇ βίᾳ τοῦ βίου. μὴ οὖν ἅψῃ τῶν δοθέντων παρὰ τοῦ θεοῦ κατὰ τὰ
αὐτῶν ἐντάλματα καὶ τὰς διδασκαλίας αὐτῶν. Kol 2,23 Ἀντὶ τοῦ ταῦτα φοβοῦ–λέγω
δὴ τὸ μὴ ἅψῃ, μὴ γεύσῃ, μηδὲ θίγῃς–λόγον τινὰ ἔχειν δοκοῦντα, ἐπειδὴ
ταπεινοφρονούντων ἐστὶ καὶ ἀφειδούντων σώματος τῷ ἐγκρατεύεσθαι ἀπὸ
βρωμάτων καὶ μὴ τιμᾶν τῇ πλησμονῇ τὴν ἰδίαν σάρκα. ἀλλ' εἰ καὶ τὸ τῆς ἐγκρατείας
καλόν, ἀλλὰ τὸ δεύτερον ἀσεβές· οὐ γὰρ μόνον ὡς κρείττους γαστρὸς ἀπέχονται,
ἀλλὰ καὶ ὡς οὐκ ὀφείλοντες ἀδικεῖν τὰ ἔμψυχα, ἃ ἐδόθη εἰς φθορὰν τῇ τοῦ βίου
ἀποχρήσει, καὶ μᾶλλον τοῦ θεοῦ ἐλεήμονες παρὰ τὰ ἄλογα εἶναι βούλονται. 327 Kol
3,3 Ἡ ζωὴ ἡμῶν κέκρυπται, ἀντὶ τοῦ ἡ μακαριότης τῆς αἰωνίου ζωῆς ἥτις πᾶσι
φανερωθήσεται, ὅταν καὶ ἡ δόξα τοῦ Χριστοῦ φανερωθῇ ἐν τῇ δευτέρᾳ αὐτοῦ
παρουσίᾳ. Kol 3,5 Ὥσπερ πολλάκις σάρκα καλεῖ τὴν ἁμαρτίαν, οὕτω καὶ μέλη τῆς
σαρκὸς νῦν καταριθμῶν πορνείαν λέγει καὶ ἀκαθαρσίαν καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς· ταῦτα γὰρ μέλη
τῆς ἁμαρτίας. Kol 3,9–10 Παλαιὸν μὲν ἄνθρωπον λέγει τὸ φρόνημα τῆς ἁμαρτίας,
μέλη δὲ τὰς πονηρὰς πράξεις· νέον δὲ ἄνθρωπον τὸ φρόνημα τὸ πνευματικόν, καὶ
μέλη αὐτοῦ τὰς ἀγαθὰς πράξεις. Σάρκα καλεῖ τὴν ἁμαρτίαν, ἧς καὶ τὰ μέλη
pass_a_gloss:
[continuing Colossians 2:20-22] ... this world nor to live as citizens in it, why do you put up with those who make decrees for you according to the way of life of this world, as though living according to it? Why, as living in the world, are you subjected to decrees: "do not taste, do not touch, do not handle," which are all for destruction in the using? These he sets out as Greek doctrines; for these people command in their own error neither to touch nor to taste anything having soul (animate). For all these things were given to human beings for destruction, that is, for destroying them and consuming them in the use and the force of life. So "do not touch" the things given by God (is) "according to their commandments and their teachings."
Colossians 2:23. In place of: fear these things, I mean "do not handle, do not taste, nor touch," which seem to have some reason, since it belongs to people who are lowly-minded and do not spare the body to abstain from foods and not to honour their own flesh with surfeit. But even if the matter of self-control is fine, yet the second (thing) is impious; for they abstain not only as superior to the belly, but also as people who must not wrong animate things, which were given for destruction in the use of life; and they want to be more merciful than God toward the irrational animals.
Colossians 3:3. "Our life is hidden," in place of: the blessedness of the eternal life, which will be revealed to all when the glory of Christ also is revealed in his second coming.
Colossians 3:5. Just as he often calls sin flesh, so also now, listing the members of the flesh, he says fornication and uncleanness and the rest; for these are members of sin.
Colossians 3:9-10. By "old man" he means the mind-set of sin, and by members the evil deeds; by "new man" the spiritual mind-set, and by its members the good deeds.
[Second form, unmarked repetition:] He calls sin flesh, whose members also [continues in the next section: he lists]
pass_b_english: … this world or to live as its citizens, why do you put up with people who lay down rules for you by the standards of this world, as if you lived by them? Why, as though you were living in the world, do you submit to rules: “Do not taste, do not touch, do not handle”, things which all perish as they are used? He presents these as Greek doctrines, for in their error these people command that no one should touch or taste anything that has life. Yet all these things were given to human beings to be used up, that is, to be spent and consumed in the use and the needs of life. So “do not touch” what God has given is a rule “according to their commandments and their teachings”.

On Colossians 2:23: This means: be wary of these rules, I mean “do not handle, do not taste, do not touch”, which seem to make some sense, because abstaining from foods and refusing to pamper one’s own flesh with plenty is the mark of people who are humble-minded and do not spare the body. But although self-control is a fine thing, their second motive is impious. They abstain not only as people who have mastered the belly, but also as people who think they must not harm living creatures, which were given to be used up in the course of life. They want to be more merciful to the dumb animals than God is.
On Colossians 3:3: “Our life is hidden” stands for the blessedness of eternal life, which will be revealed to all when the glory of Christ is also revealed at his second coming.
On Colossians 3:5: Just as he often calls sin “flesh”, so now, listing the members of the flesh, he names fornication, uncleanness and the rest; for these are the members of sin.
On Colossians 3:9–10: By “the old man” he means the mind set on sin, and by its members, evil deeds; by “the new man” he means the spiritual mind, and by its members, good deeds.

lemmas.gloss: lay down rules; be subjected to rules (Colossians 2:20)
for perishing; in the using, consumption
superior to the belly, masters of appetite

choices.term: μὴ οὖν ἅψῃ τῶν δοθέντων παρὰ τοῦ θεοῦ κατὰ τὰ αὐτῶν ἐντάλματα καὶ τὰς διδασκαλίας αὐτῶν
choices.english: So “do not touch” what God has given is a rule “according to their commandments and their teachings”.
choices.why: Severian joins 2:21 ('do not touch') to 2:22 ('according to the commandments and teachings of men'); the old English made it a command of Paul ('Therefore, do not touch the things given by God').
rejected: Therefore, do not touch the things given by God according to their own commandments and their teachings (old)

choices.term: ἐν τῇ ἀποχρήσει καὶ τῇ βίᾳ τοῦ βίου
choices.english: in the use and the needs of life
choices.why: βία ('force, violence') makes poor sense; read as the pressing needs of life, perhaps for χρείᾳ. Recorded in translator_notes.

choices.term: μᾶλλον τοῦ θεοῦ ἐλεήμονες παρὰ τὰ ἄλογα εἶναι βούλονται
choices.english: They want to be more merciful to the dumb animals than God is.
choices.why: μᾶλλον τοῦ θεοῦ = 'more than God'; παρὰ τὰ ἄλογα = toward the beasts. The old 'merciful to God contrary to reason' reversed it.
rejected: they wish to be merciful to God contrary to reason (old)

choices.term: Ἀντὶ τοῦ ταῦτα φοβοῦ … λόγον τινὰ ἔχειν δοκοῦντα
choices.english: This means: be wary of these rules … which seem to make some sense
choices.why: ἀντὶ τοῦ introduces Severian's paraphrase of 2:23 ('which have a show of wisdom'); the old English turned it into 'Instead of fearing these things'.

choices.term: Σάρκα καλεῖ τὴν ἁμαρτίαν, ἧς καὶ τὰ μέλη | καταριθμεῖ …
choices.english: The second catena form adds: He calls sin “flesh”, and he also lists its …
choices.why: Start of an unmarked repetition of the 3:5 and 3:9–10 notes (SOURCE_ISSUES item 1: 'the old and new man'), running on into u02-rem-close. Its opening clause repeats 3:5 but is kept because the sentence runs across the section break.
SOURCE_ISSUES item 4: the section is filed under chapter 2 though half is on 3:3–10; each note now carries its own label.
